newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - US experts eye housing starts Sept 16 wk.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - US experts eye housing starts Sept 16 wk.

text.p: Smooth sailing rather than stormy seas is the most appropriate metaphor to describe market reaction to next week's relatively uneventful data calendar, economists said on Friday.
In a Reuters survey on Friday, U.S. economists forecast few if any data surprises next week and predicted that housing starts would be the key indicator to watch.
Peter Kretzmer, an economist at NationsBanc Capital Markets Inc, said the only data monetary policy makers and financial institutions will be watching is housing starts.
On average, respondents forecast August housing starts at 1.445 million, a whisker of a drop from the previous month's reading of 1.46 million.

Jonathan Basile, an economist at HSBC Securities Inc, said next week's economic reports will be inconsequential to Federal Reserve monetary policy makers, but did note that industrial production and initial jobless claims data could act as important gauges of inflation pressure.
"The capacity utilization numbers...and also the claims numbers are important, because we're starting to see an upward trend from August," Basile said.

On average, economists forecast August industrial production would have risen 0.4 percent from its previous 0.1 percent climb. Capacity use was forecast to have inched up to 83.3 from 83.2 percent last month.

Basile also said that the Philly Fed is going to give the first read on what the National Association of Purchasing Managers may be in September and the "market is always looking for something that's forward-looking."
